# Reviewed Pine engine sources

EdgeLab pins PineTS 0.11.0 under AGPL-3.0-only. The original npm package stays unchanged. `scripts/pine-engine.mjs` reconstructs its exact readable sources from the packaged browser source map and applies the reviewed files in `overrides/`. The missing, type-only Indicator barrel comes from the pinned package's declaration re-exports.

`manifest.json` seals the installed version, source-map bytes, declaration barrel, original source bytes and each modified file with SHA-256. Development and production workers use the same source resolver. A changed dependency or patch fails the build until its source and hashes are reviewed together. Imports resolve only to the verified sources and three bundled MIT dependencies; there is no network fetch or arbitrary disk fallback.

The local changes preserve `varip` declarations and object-field metadata, and provide an explicit indicator-only realtime lifecycle for deterministic engine tests. Compiler-generated type metadata retains the upstream type registry and correct method receiver name, including overloaded methods. Ordinary mutable values roll back between updates; intrabar-persistent values and fields retain their appropriate state. Provisional outputs replace the current bar. `setRealtimeMode(true)` is required before `run`; `updateTail(context, { confirmed: false })` recalculates an open bar and `{ confirmed: true }` closes it. Provider bars must remain chronological. Streaming, paginated realtime and strategy tick scheduling are unsupported and fail explicitly.

The application still executes closed snapshots. The engine API does not establish live chart integration or TradingView parity. Tests cover supported scalar, collection and declared UDT field rollback, moving-average state and provisional output replacement. Full drawing-object behavior and per-tick performance budgets are not established. Member and type-factory UDT copies use current declared fields, preserve absent/undefined values, and retain shallow references to collections and other objects. See `backend/tests/pine-object-copy55.test.js` for copying tests, `pine-realtime54.test.js` for actual minified-engine lifecycle tests and `pine-engine-integrity54.test.js` for build integrity tests.

Historical object-field receivers are lowered as values in plotting arguments and function returns. Pine v6 uses `(object[offset]).field`; direct field history on registered UDT receivers is rejected with a corrective diagnostic. Pine v5 and JavaScript inputs retain their existing compatibility paths. `backend/tests/pine-object-history56.test.js` verifies existing historical receivers, custom offsets, copied and nested objects, reference identity, typed methods and explicit realtime lifecycle updates. First-bar field access through an absent object is not established by these tests.

Explicit realtime sessions can initialize an entirely closed dataset with `setRealtimeMode(true, { initialTail: "historical" })`. Those bars execute once as confirmed history; the next explicit appended bar starts realtime execution. The default `initialTail: "open"` retains the provisional final-bar behavior.

Realtime rollback state has hard limits of 16,384 mutable nodes, 262,144 mutable cells and 1,280,000 Series slots. Trusted callers may select smaller positive integer limits through `limits: { nodes, cells, seriesSlots }`. Exceeding a limit raises `REALTIME_STATE_LIMIT` and halts that session. Discarded newborn rollback records are released after restoration while historical references, aliases and surviving intrabar state remain available. These are snapshot-state limits, not a total heap or execution-time guarantee: scripts and the underlying engine can allocate memory before snapshot checks. `backend/tests/pine-realtime57.test.js` covers retention, limits and closed-history initialization. The application still uses closed snapshots.

Field-level intrabar persistence follows the [Pine objects documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/objects/): a persistent object reference does not exempt its ordinary fields from rollback. Excluding discarded newborn field qualifiers from persistence discovery is a local retention policy; TradingView equivalence for discarded-object aliases is not established.

Modified files retain the original LuxAlgo copyright and AGPL notices, with an EdgeLab modification notice. Matching source distributions must include these overrides, manifest, build script and the locked dependency sources. See the repository licence and third-party notices.
